Kernfs node, dentry and superblock lifetime beyond creation and destruction calls.
Css release, populated tracking and css set linking internals.
Notifier chain subscribers and offline drain behavior.
Per processor backlog insertion sites and ordering guarantees.

findings.text: Hierarchy root setup initializes the root lifetime reference, preallocates css set links, allocates a hierarchy identifier, creates a deactivated kernfs root, populates its directory and statistics, binds requested subsystems, announces online lifetime, then publishes the root and links it into every css set.
Hierarchy identity uses cyclic allocation from a global identifier space stored on the root, with a matching removal that releases the identifier when setup fails or the root is torn down.

Statistics flushing walks every possible processor, drains pending updates under an interrupt safe subsystem lock, and invokes either base or subsystem handlers, while exit flushes first and then frees per processor state after verifying no pending links remain.

Effective state lookup climbs from a group toward its parents for the nearest attached subsystem state and falls back to the initial set when none is found, with one form returning a borrowed pointer and another returning a referenced online state under read side protection.

File operations resolve the target state from the kernfs private group and file type, using the subsystem slot when subsystem configuration and a file subsystem exist and otherwise using the group self state, relying on drain guarantees to keep the result valid during the operation.

Base accounting combines user time, system time, execution runtime, notification count and optionally force idle totals, and a per processor flush propagates deltas from local samples into group totals and then into parent totals when the parent is not the ultimate root.

Version one task lookup scans hierarchy roots for a matching identifier and returns a referenced group or a not found marker, while early initialization creates a single active per processor workqueue for pid list destruction.

A newly set up root has inode number one, its ancestor slot zero pointing to itself, exactly one group counted, and an empty child list at publication time, with double the observed css set count preallocated for linking.
Only self states and subsystems that provide a flush handler participate in statistics tracking, and exit is a no operation when participation is absent or per processor storage was never allocated.

Pending statistics form bottom up per processor trees where a marked node implies all ancestors are marked, termination is parent self or self self, and flush collection unlinks the root from its parent before ordering the root ahead of descendants.

The default hierarchy root uses statically allocated per processor statistics and base statistics storage rather than dynamically allocated blocks, with visibility and subsystem masks tracked in dedicated globals.
Root setup and hierarchy identifier allocation and release require the global cgroup mutex to be held by the caller, asserted on entry.
Linking a new root into all css sets and updating populated state holds the interrupt safe css set spinlock, and task hierarchy lookup nests that spinlock inside read side protection.
Generic cgroup identifier removal serializes with a dedicated bottom half safe spinlock around the identifier removal.

Statistics update processing and flush list construction hold one interrupt safe spinlock selected by subsystem, reacquired separately for each processor to bound disabled interrupt time, with construction asserting the same lock is held.

Effective referenced lookup and task hierarchy lookup hold read side critical sections while dereferencing subsystem slots and root lists, with reference acquisition attempted before leaving the section.

Hierarchy root state observed here comprises an embedded root group, a kernfs root pointer, a numeric hierarchy identifier, a membership list node, and a group count, with the embedded group carrying its node pointer, ancestor table, lifetime reference and statistics storage.

Per processor statistics nodes carry sibling and child linkage for pending updates, a lockless backlog node with an owner back pointer, and a separate flush ordering pointer used only while the subsystem lock is held.

Base statistics comprise processor times, execution runtime, notification count and optionally force idle total, mirrored in per processor current, last and subtree accumulators plus group totals and last snapshots.

Subsystem metadata is built from a repeated include that generates a pointer table, a name table, and enabled plus default hierarchy key tables, with per subsystem enabled keys exported for external checks.

Root establishment proceeds through reference initialization, link preallocation, identifier allocation, kernfs creation, directory population, statistics initialization and subsystem rebinding, where any failure before publication unwinds only already acquired resources in reverse order and no failure is permitted after the lifetime announcement.

Statistics progress from lockless per subsystem backlog insertion to bottom up pending tree formation and finally to a level ordered flush list consumed under lock, with the backlog drained at the start of collection for the requested subsystem.

Version one mount acquisition checks privilege, drains offline groups, selects a root and attempts a live reference under lock, then builds the tree outside the lock and restarts the system call after a short delay when a live reference was unavailable or the root began dying.

Version one filesystem mount is entered with a filesystem context, requires system administration capability in the caller namespace, and returns either a populated tree, a permission or internal error, or a restart request after delay.

Tree construction selects a magic value by filesystem type, obtains the kernfs tree, substitutes the namespace root group entry when inside a non initial cgroup namespace, and releases the extra root reference when no new superblock was created.

Early boot options disable version one support globally, for named hierarchies, or for named subsystems by token list, and separately control whether process listings show all entries through a boolean flag.

Statistics flush is exposed as a BPF callable that safely ignores nonparticipating states, and base flushing calls a weak overridable hook per group parent and processor that defaults to no operation.

Setup warns when the root inode is not one or lifetime notification reports an error, and enforces emptiness of the root child list and a group count of one, while flush exit warns when per processor pending links are inconsistent and abandons teardown.

Flush may sleep and yields between processors, so it must not be called from non sleepable or long interrupt disabled regions, and its per processor lock acquisition traces contention before blocking.
Version one pid list destruction workqueue creation during early initialization treats allocation failure as fatal.
Maximum control file name length equals maximum type name length plus maximum file type name length plus two separator characters.
Minimum file notification interval is the number of timer ticks per second divided by one hundred and rounded up.
Optional mount feature set optionally includes pressure support with a fixed literal name when that configuration is enabled, tracked by a disable mask.
